name: The Residences at Mandarin Oriental, Miami — North Tower
notes: HEIGHT NOT RECORDED, and the reason is worth keeping. FAA case 2026-ASO-7022-OE establishes the North Tower at 446 ft above ground against 455 to 470 ft above sea level, but states it ONLY in a coordinate table whose above-ground versus above-sea-level split lives in a column header, with no prose sentence tying a figure to a basis — unlike companion case 2026-ASO-7021-OE for the South Tower, which carries the sentence: the proposed building project consists of four points at height of 852 and 856 feet AGL, 861 and 865 feet AMSL. Confirmed by running one extractor over both letters: the six prose patterns present in 7021 return zero hits in 7022, because 7022 is a four-page letter with no additional-information page and therefore neither the narrative nor the AGL glossary. The 446 ft figure is sound and is kept here for reference; it is simply not quotable to the standard the height field requires. The alternative was the press line giving previously reported heights of 850 and 426 feet respectively, which would have passed validation because it mentions no sea level at all — and was deliberately refused: it is a design figure with no stated above-ground basis, sits 20 ft below the FAA's measured figure, is hedged by the outlet as previously reported, and is only recoverable by pairing numbers across a respectively. Storing it would put a figure of unknown basis into a field that means feet above ground, which is a worse failure than an empty cell. The superseded 2022 filing for this tower does carry the prose form, at 691 ft above ground or 700 ft above sea level, but that was an over-filed placeholder the 2026 refiling replaced.
